qualifying_findings.title: WSP MCP WordPress connector exposes unpublished post excerpts through broken access control
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: WSP MCP AI Agents Connector for WordPress through 2.9.5 registers wsp_get_posts with no capability requirement, accepts any logged-in user at its MCP endpoint, and honours status=all without author or ownership filtering. A Subscriber-or-higher user can read metadata and 40-word excerpts for draft, pending, and scheduled posts.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Primary CVE Services record with linked Wordfence advisory and public WordPress source/change evidence; in-window publication; broken MCP-tool authorization and confidential-content disclosure.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: bilalnaseer WSP MCP – Free MCP Plugin for WordPress: Connect Claude, ChatGPT & AI Agents, versions through 2.9.5; wsp_get_posts capability, endpoint authentication, and post-status/ownership authorization boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An authenticated agent or plugin user must be authorized at each MCP tool and data-query boundary. Session authentication alone cannot justify broad retrieval of unpublished content, especially when agent tools accept caller-controlled query scopes.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad WordPress plugin and MCP connector product context is upstream-owned.
Per-tool authorization, data minimization, and confidential-content disclosure implications are locally owned.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High: the primary record specifies affected versions, the precise authorization path, affected roles, and disclosed fields. The record does not state a fixed version; verify the linked change before durable remediation guidance.

qualifying_findings.title: JetBrains Junie CLI executes MCP configuration from an untrusted project
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: JetBrains Junie CLI before 26.8.3 could execute code through an untrusted project's MCP server configuration. The public CVE record identifies 26.8.3 as the first unaffected version.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Primary JetBrains-assigned CVE Services record; in-window publication; untrusted repository configuration leading to local code execution.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: JetBrains Junie CLI earlier than 26.8.3; project-supplied MCP server configuration trust boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Repository-provided agent configuration is executable supply-chain input. Opening or reviewing untrusted code must not activate its MCP servers without a distinct trust decision and a release gate that enforces it.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad Junie and MCP product context is upstream-owned.
General repository-review and coding-agent workflows are upstream-owned.
Untrusted-project configuration execution and MCP supply-chain control implications are locally owned.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for the published affected-version boundary and code-execution claim. The concise CNA record has no detailed exploit narrative; ingest should capture JetBrains' fixed-issue note before extending operational guidance.

qualifying_findings.title: Claude Agent SDK resume argument injection bypasses SDK permission controls
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Claude Agent SDK for Python before 0.2.121 passes resume as a separate Claude CLI token without validation. If an application supplies an attacker-controlled, dash-prefixed session ID, it can inject --mcp-config, define a stdio MCP server, and execute its command at CLI startup outside the SDK's permission controls. Version 0.2.121 fixes the issue.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Primary GitHub CNA CVE Services record, GitHub Security Advisory, vendor advisory, and release; in-window CVE/GitHub Advisory Database publication; argument injection leading to MCP-mediated arbitrary command execution.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: anthropics claude-agent-sdk-python / claude-agent-sdk package before 0.2.121; application-controlled resume session identifier to Claude CLI argv and MCP configuration boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A model or user-facing session value must not become a configuration or command-line authority channel. SDK permission controls cannot compensate for unsafe argument construction that lets an attacker install an MCP server before those controls execute.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad Claude Agent SDK and Claude CLI product context is upstream-owned.
General coding-agent SDK integration and workflow usage are upstream-owned.
CLI argument construction, injected MCP configuration, and permission-boundary bypass implications are locally owned.
